about: The `targetexpr` of a <send> is a string computed from the machine's fields when the send runs, held to the routes the document declares as `sce:targets`: the send goes by the entry that matches, and a value in none of them is error.communication with nothing sent. `route` holds `#_internal` to begin with, so `fire` (declaring `#_internal` and `#_parent`) delivers `landed` to this session; `narrow` declares `#_parent` alone, so the same value is refused although the machine could send by it. A machine with no parent cannot send to one, so the declared `#_parent` is error.communication too, and so is a value no send declares. Expected values are derived from the document, not observed from a backend.

steps.note: the route the machine holds is a declared one: the event is delivered to this session
and again: the send reads the route each time it runs
this send declares `#_parent` alone: `#_internal` is a route the machine can send by, and a value this send does not declare is refused
the route changes to the parent; nothing is sent
a declared route that no session answers at: this machine has no parent
the route changes to a session nothing declares
a value in none of the declared routes is an address nobody is at: reported, and nothing delivered
the route is a declared one again, and the machine goes on
